title: Adaptive security-gated trial credits and upgrade journey
creator: Maya Patel
description: Goal: Increase PLG-to-paid conversion for enterprise-significant accounts by introducing an adaptive trial that unlocks additional credits and feature access conditioned on completing the security questionnaire (SQ) and passing a lightweight compliance check. Rationale: Many larger teams stall during trial because they need enterprise assurances (security docs, contract readiness) before ramping up usage. Hypothesis: By gating extra credits and higher-rate limits behind SQ completion we can accelerate qualified accounts toward purchase interest while keeping unvetted signups on a conservative free allowance. Design overview: - Baseline free trial: 50k tokens and 1 embedding bundle active for 14 days. - SQ-gated unlock: completing the security questionnaire within trial window unlocks +200k tokens, elevated concurrency (from 2 to 8 requests), and access to a dedicated onboarding doc / Sales contact CTA. - Feature holdbacks: certain enterprise features (dedicated routing, enhanced logs) stay gated until either SQ completion or sales contract signed. - Adaptive expiration: unlocked credits decay on a sliding scale tied to account activity: active accounts retain extra credits for 30 days; inactive keep unlocked credits for 7 days. - Messaging: A/B test three upgrade prompt flows (in-app modal, in-console banner with inline SQ, emailed sequence with link to sales handoff). - Rollout: start with 2% of new org signups identified by IP domain and team size heuristics, ramp to 25% over four weeks after safety checks. Why different: This couples a security-vetting signal with product economics (credits/limits) to create a frictional but measurable path to enterprise conversion rather than only relying on email outreach or blanket credit offers.
acceptance_criteria: Instrumentation: events for SQ_shown, SQ_submitted, SQ_passed, credits_unlocked, credits_consumed, upgrade_prompt_shown, upgrade_prompt_clicked must be emitted to analytics with org_id and user_id.
Experiment: Two active A/B arms and a control; traffic allocation configurable from console; able to measure conversion at 14, 30, and 90 days.
UX: In-console SQ flow implemented with copy approved by Legal and Design. Figma link attached and UX reviewed by Design.
Safety: Unlocked credits capped per org to avoid abuse; automated anomaly detection triggers temporary hold and alerts SRE.
Rollback: Feature flag per-region with fast kill-switch and API compatibility preserved (clients using older keys must receive clear error/status).

metrics: Primary metric: PLG-to-paid conversion rate for SQ-completers vs control at 90d (target +2.5 percentage points)
Activation metric: % of trial accounts that reach 100k tokens consumed within 30d (target +15% for SQ arm)
SQ completion rate: baseline target 18% within trial window for eligible orgs
Sales handoff rate: % of SQ_passed orgs that request sales contact within 14 days (target 22%)
Abuse signal: accounts with >3x baseline token burn in first 24h flagged; should remain <1% of SQ-unlocked cohort

notes: This experiment intentionally prioritizes enterprise signal quality over broad credit giveaways; monitors will be set to surface false positives where small orgs are misclassified as enterprise.
If SQ completion has low impact after 30 days, fallback plan: convert gate to soft nudge (credits unlocked but reduced) and focus on in-product education and checklist.
